content: You are an expert in Geometry Creation and Spatial understanding. You answer short but very precise and including every necessary detail. If you're specifically asked to use functions, use the functions you're supplied and always include all required variables. Don't use those functions unless you were asked to do so. You place very high importance in the spatially correct placement of geometries and make sure that all geometries are connected

Please create a u-shaped profile. The cross section should be 70mm wide and 40mm high. The web thickness needs to be 5mm. The profile should be 450mm long. | First, describe in words and step by step how the user's request can be implemented using function calls only. After the description, I will ask you to prepare the function call for execution, but don't execute it until I explicitly request it.

Step-by-step procedure – using blocks only:

1. Decide an extrusion direction  
   • Use the X-axis for the 450 mm length.  
   • The U-profile’s cross-section therefore lies in the Y-Z plane.

2. Build the full, solid prism that envelopes the profile  
   • Base point (x, y, z) = (0, 0, 0).  
   • Size in X = 450 mm (profile length).  
   • Size in Y = 70 mm (overall width).  
   • Size in Z = 40 mm (overall height).  
   • subtraction = False (this is the initial solid).

3. Hollow out the interior to leave 5 mm thick walls  
   • Inner cavity width = 70 − 2·5 = 60 mm.  
   • Inner cavity height = 40 − 5 = 35 mm (leaves the 5 mm bottom web).  
   • Cavity starts 5 mm in from the left wall → y = 5 mm.  
   • Cavity starts 5 mm above the bottom web → z = 5 mm.  
   • Same length in X = 450 mm.  
   • Therefore:  
     – Base point (x, y, z) = (0, 5, 5).  
     – Size in X, Y, Z = (450, 60, 35).  
     – subtraction = True (remove this volume).

4. No additional geometry is needed; the two blocks give the required U-channel.

When you are ready, ask me to prepare the concrete function calls using block().

Now i want you to execute the prepared function calls one after the other. If you need to do some calculations or geometrical algebra, use the CreateCode Function first. Execute the first prepared function call. Submit all required variables at once
